Our question here calls on the contributions of famous fictional and factual human characters, who are interpreted in the contexts of Existentialism and Epigenesis. These topics will be discussed in the following paper. The Learning Mode used here will be the (Gregorc 1971-5), Abstract Sequential in an autodidact variant (any meaning in these words?) To initiate a discussion of the relationship between Existentialism and Epigenesis, first consider some specific cases, a few "factual" and the remainder "fictional" derived from writings popular at the time they were created - that popularity unabated since their diverse origins. Initial emphasis is placed on the "pulp character," Clarke "Doc" Savage, renowned by the writings of Lester Dent. 

What is Epigenesis? And Existentialism? Existentialism  is an expression of dissatisfaction with the structure and function of the world from the view point of human expectations. Epigenesis is a scientific enterprise to derive the influences on the Mendellian factors whose function appears influenced by endogenous and exogenous factors.  

Here, the technique of Deconstruction in the sense of J. Derrida (1967).will intrude. Those familiar with the scientific conceptions of Reductionism will understand immediately this warning.. So, in Science, at which level of structure will a matter be investigated? At the most superficial "macroscopic level" or the ultimate "microscopic level?'" The ultimate microscopic levels demand the manipulation of information by a non-mathematical physics as yet not elucidated, but essential for the description of the neuronal, microtubule functions. (See Roger Penrose, Consciousness and the Universe, (2010) for the meaning of this phrase.) At these lowest levels macroscopic properties seem to "disappear" since they are emergent properties not linked to any single, compositional unit.

The relationship between the genotype (microscopic) and its expressed  phenotype (macroscopic) is particularly complex, and goes so far beyond the treatments in elementary texts that "the reality" seems a different subject.  For an in depth treatment see the (27 Septmber 2019) special issue of Science where the SNPS (the commonest form of genetic variation where one nucleotide replaces another) are used as indicators of disease susceptibility and the inheritance of  other characters such as eye color. The included articles are based on the GWAS (genome wide association study) technique - where hundreds of thousands of SNPS were located throughout  individual cell genomes. The revealed presence of these SNPS provides the basis of inferred phenotypic characters, without reference to parental origins. Such studies have included sample sizes of one million, identifying thousands of gene variations affecting hundreds of human traits - one in partciular predicts educational success complicated by parental associations. Such predictions are confounded by environmental epigenetic factors in the containing cell and its surroundings. Although this genetic and environmental variability produce the phenotype, the  relationship between the effect of each factor is somewhat blurred.

Similarly, in Deconstruction a statement in the "French language" is about to be translated from French to English,  Are some "emergent properties" lost in the process? Do the original letters carry information lost by other letters or words from French to English - is "something" always lost? And, suppose that the English translations erase the intentions of the French. What then? The French is irreplaceable. And, if the statement was originally "spoken," are emergent properties lost when the statement is heard in a different voice? Therefore, if documents of special meaning to humanity are recorded the language and the voice would be of great significance. Which version of James Joyce's  Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man should be studied - the original or final version of the author? Incidentally, did Joyce compose this work in a "private, personal as yet untranslatable language?" Of what value are the edited versions appearing subsequently from scholars? For further details see J. Derrida, De la Grammatologie.(1967), (not 1968, a translation). Now, who is Doc Savage? Or more properly, “What is Clarke Savage, Jr.?” Savage might have replied, "Who do they say that I am?" From the facts provided in the “Man of Bronze.” and “The Arctic Treasure,” and repeated in the subsequent novels, Clarke Savage, Jr. was developed under close supervision and tutelage of Clarke Savage, Sr. into what his father considered the “Supreme Adventurer.” By what means were his son’s distinctive physical and mental characteristics (including hair, eyes and skin pigmentation and texture, acute senses and intellect) developed in him alone, if not being inherited from any other variations of the human specimens found throughout the world?" Here Epigenesis enters significantly, and Existentialism as well, as to how and what are the most beneficent choices to make? Amber eyes, for example, are extremely rare, occurring in only .01% of humans. Extant since earliest human origins, the trait is derived from the presence of eumelanin and pheomelanin and their interactions in Rayleigh scattering. The origin of the amber eye trait not derived from whole genes (thank Mendel and Morgan) but single nucleotide polymorphism. On the British Isles the trait is common among the Irish.  How could all of these attributes have develope by education and physical culture? 

Specifically, Savage is a much improved version his father. As discussed elsewhere, Savage Sr with his unbrideled wealth, had developed a private institution, The Fortress of Solitude at a secret location in the Arctic - reputed to have been one and a half acre cavity under the ice, reached from a cylindrical transport reached at the surface. Here he collected the finest scientific minds of the time, and freed of societal restrictions they were allowed to seek the fruits of their imaginations. In effect, they created a New World freed of the influence of disabling, religious, legal and other restrictions for orignal creativity. The Fortress by native accounts was destroyed in a cataclysm taken place in the 1946 - 1950 period. Originally, under these conditions scientific understandings advanced  at an unprecidented rate. None of these achievements were formally published. The "outside world" was considered an failed enterprise. (One creation of these laboratories was the original techniques of Gene Manipulation, now known as CRSPR, in 1923 by Esquerra Forteau and his colleagues. Further, evidence has appeared suggesting NGS, AFLP, PCR, Microassay and GWAS - including a compendium of other reachniques were also within their grasp. Particularly significant to this paper is the technique of DNA Phenotyping, where DNA is used to predict a human's physical characteristics, age, and ancestry.  These techniques transformed Doc Savage Sr into a supreme CLONE,  the incipient Doc Savage Jr  of near superhuman capabilities, inconceivable by Darwin's Natural Selection even given unlimited time.

For the mathematically inclined, facial features are identified geometric ratios, rather than the whole, "nose" for example. Discussed elsewhere  is the conception that a "face" is constructed by the brain by two procedures - a. geometry outline, followed by, b. addition of details (based on appealing mathematical ratios).   

These ideas developed as an extension of the belief that "No life is satisfacrtory and evolves into the desire to have done something different."  Here Epigenesis enters significantly, and Existentialism as well, as to how and what are the most beneficent choices to make. and then manipulated by the team in the Arctic Fortress, considered even today as unprecedented science of thought leading to metarepresentation.. 

The discussion above reveals two antithetical philosophies regarding humans existing in the world and the consequences they produce on adoption: 

1. Doc Savage - Philosophic/Scientific Materialism: The world is incomplete. The role of humans is to change the world into a more hospitable place of existence. Education can extend human capacities, and Science can reveal procedures beyond superstition and other forms of ignorance for human benefits. 

2. Mary Shelley - Romantic Necessitarianism and Associativism: Science and technology obscure associations with Nature – the surest and most effective means for the development of a healthy mentality. Schooling and other formatted procedures cannot replace the effects of associated chance occurrences in nature and the innate antecedent elements of the mind producing personal reaction to these occurrences expressed almost exclusively in artistic creations. Lacking these encounters produces an empty identity.

 

One subsidiary purpose in writing this review was to compare the Doc Savage novels to what is commonly referred to as “literature.” Great forms of literature are often identified as the works of Shakespeare. Is “The Man of Bronze” as even Lester Dent suggested not valuable beyond a paycheck? Dent may have written the novels in a "Dream State," where his ideas simply "appeared from archetypes" and they should have been considered, "prescient" rather than "pulp." In effect, Doc Savage’s life seems to be existentially superior to that of Macbeth who proclaims - Human life is “…a tale told by an idiot – full of sound and fury signifying nothing….” Compare this statement to -

                                     The Doc Savage Creed:

 "Let me strive every moment of my life, to make myself better and better, to the best of my ability, that all may profit by it. Let me think of the right and lend all my assistance to those who need it, with no regard for anything but justice. Let me take what comes with a smile, without loss of courage."

Could Macbeth or even Shakespeare himself have benefitted from Doc Savage’s mind- altering operations?

Suggested here is the premise that Doc Savage, Jr. is actually a very much-improved clone of his father, improved by purposeful, scientific, epigenetic procedures rather than selection of chance events over geologic time. 

Consider Savage's appearance and behavior and their epigenetic origin - Handsome, well muscled, and one would guess attracted to females and aggressive to men. His interactions with felons and females are not what one would expect. He never killed adversaries, but lulled them to sleep with anesthetic, "mercy bullets". He avoided emotional contacts with women, all too willing to accept them. His "Creed" suggests he was anything but an aggressive, "territorial male."

How did this come about? Remember, emergent properties "evaporate" at the microscopic level of structure, to be replaced by the reprentations of cellular, then molecular primary representations. Also, the language changes. Here, this structure the Hypothalamus, influenced by reports of the sense organs as to the nature of external surroundings, in response stimulates a much smaller structure, the pituitary gland by way of a hormone GTRH  (gonadotropin releasing hormone) and the pituitary releases a GT hormone (gonadotropin) in response. The gonads (here testes) then are stimulated to secrete another hormone, testosterone which alters the behavior of other organs with suitable chemical receptors. Thus, the Male Characteristics - musculature, aggressiveness, etc. are brought about. Savage Sr. modified this scheme such that what he considered desirable features were retained and the less desirable were modified physically and chemically, or eliminated.

Erskine escaped from the lab, later to be assassinated by a Hydra Agent, Heinz Kruger. For further details see the latest comic series - late  2023-2024. As with most significant events, their history is replete with apocryphal versions. What were the epigenetic effects transforming Steve Rogers, into Captain America who donned the American flag as his uniform?

The fusion of the Psyche and Material Reality was the goal of the physicist, Wolfgag Pauli and the Psychologist, Carl Gustav Jung (1865 - 1961) for many years in correspondences. They relied on the content of dreams, which they considered an access to the subconscious mind. They did not admit to "meta-representations" in their thinking as discussed in earlier paragraphs. The original representation was sought rather than than that  derived from a superficial metarepresentation drawing attention to itself. Freud suggested the subconscious without experimental verification - a baseless metarepresentation resulted. Werner Heisenberg pointed out, "There are ideas that light up images in the human mind without reference to external reality..." Using mathematics, Pauli contributed to the Four Quantum Numbers; specifically the numbers  necessary to describe an electron in an atom - The Principal (energy of the electron) Azimuthal - (horizontal direction) Magnetic - (the orbitals and their orientation) Spin - ((orientation within an orbital.)  From his meetings with Pauli and the analysis of a "thousand" of Pauli's dreams, Jung  conceded there must be Four Archetypes describing the Psyche - Anima (female component) Animus (male component) Shadow (unresolved relationships) Self - (consolidation of all). These four represented by the Mandela symbol, as the Universe in its most perfect form.

In spite of their disdain for metarepresentations, Pauli and and Jung should have recognized the human body as a complex animatronic device - constructed by the metabolism to include all properties even the subconscious mind which they sought to isolate. The metbolism and its constituent structural and functional elements are therefore the basis of all human qualities and are metsrepresentations functioning together the ultimate goal being the replication of the constituent nucleic acids.

This messenger combines with receptor sites in cells with available receptors.  The receptive cells are abundant and wide spread in the human and other animal bodies. Stress occurs as the number of these sites are affected by the cortisol. To lessen this stress response, some of these receptors must be "quieted". How are the contentions listed above to be interpreted? Considering that 99% of life forms once existing on Earth have been eliminated, the concept of "Purpose" must be dropped. The replacement might be, "Chance;" where the creatures of earth's history are the results of a process of descent with modification, where a fortunate few survive the rigors of change in the Earth's environment. This change applies also to the tissues, organs and systems of an organism since their development was not based on a preordained "plan." The driving force is in fact the unique power if nucleic acids in self replication. Another contention to be eliminated is "Progress," since this idea suggests "advancement toward some goal." An epigenetic idea current at this time is that when clusters of genes mutate, yet remain "silent" until the mutation of an another gene (or genes?) turns them on. and, instead of an incremental evolutionary change, a new kind of organism is created, without incremental steps. This idea is useful since it accounts for the lack of many "transitional forms" in the geologic record. The new organism might find an environment in which it can survive - if it does so it survives; if not, it is eliminated. Such a process resembles that of "Epigenesis" whereby an embryo develops from an."undifferentiated' fertilized egg". Here, in some cases the genes themselves are not altered; instead, the manner the information in them is read is altered. Another phenomenon expressed most vividly in Lichens is the Composite Organism. Here, the lichen is composed of two subunits derived from distinctly different evolutionary histories - a Fungus and an Alga, The two units retain their individuality, (they can be grown separately in culture flasks). As a composite, the fungus has "stolen" certain genes from the alga and can, thereby, manipulate its metabolism.There is also evidence that animal bodies (including humans) have a similar arrangement. Flagellated cells in at least some cases are genetically different from the majority of cells composing the body of the host - suggesting a lichen-like arrangement. Further, these genetically  different units come across "whole' rather than created from constituents at the time of fertilization and enbryogenesis. Microchimeral Inheritancs is another contributing factor - Here, the human egg is a chimera of cells where in the cytoplasm of that egg are cells derived from humans in the family history including mother, female relatives, including grandparents .During morphogenesis these inherited cells contribute to the structures and functions of organs as they did in ancestral individuals. Certain organelles including mitochondria are inherited whole with their reduced genetics in place. Are fanciful stories, "lies" humans enjoy better than reality? How often is a "lie" contain the kernel of an  undiscovered truth?

Consider - "Schrodinger's Cat"  Fact or fiction? If you merely believe it, does that make it coercive? 

Smart's life (a test of his reasoning) was disappointing with a failed marriage and imprisonment for unpaid debts. Though his work was essentially ignored at the time, of late it is viewed with increasing esteem. Why?  Political correctness?  A consideration here might be to ask, are "beauty" or "best work" illusions as applied to the conception of "free will?" Does "beauty" exist independently of human considerations? 

Smart was not the only literaturist who wrote after losing some of his "marbles." When Charles Dickens went walking, he carried a stick to to brush aside the gremlins dancing on the pavement before him.  

Overheard at a publishing house as a committee reviews a book for publication - "Is there an audience for this kind of thing?" If so, there is money to be made - perhaps the most important of literary consideration. The origins of the works (obsessions or compulsions of the authors) need not be considered except to add the allure of mystique to attract a susceptible audience. 

Might we close with mention of another possibility? The authors of the stories based on super heroes including Savage, Holmes, Ray, Tarzan,  Frankenstein, and all the others mentioned here, written by authors that did not take them seriously are supreme examples of satire and parody of extant Humans. Jonathan Swift wrotes regarding his satirical Gulliver's Travels (1726), that  he wrote the stories to "vex the world rather than divert it.." If these authors and their creations were designed to annoy the world and its paradigms of skill and virtue then we might draw this conclusion as necessary. Another example is the well known series for young people, namely The Hardy Boys, written by "ghost writers," including Leslie McFarlane, for the sole purpose of "money" used for buying the  "current month's ration of coal." Even his young son who bought and read them as they came out was astonished when he discovered his father was the author of his "favorites." How could ridicule of style and characters not creep in if McFarlane was forced to write this "trivia" when his aspirations were so much higher?

The revision of the Joker and Batman histories by. Zdarsky follows the pattern of many famous personalities, where an authority with few facts embellishes to make the characters more or less appealing.  Was a witness present when a bat flew in the window of his dressing room inspiring Bruce Wayne to adopt the persona of a bat? Zdarsky plans to fill in the years (?) between the deaths of Wayne's parents and his appearance as The Bat Man or BATMAN. {Which is it?} 

Now for a different tact - A reader even with only passing familiarity with Zdarsky, notes his bemused, facial expressions and reactions to interviewers, Under the guise of new details on the history of Batman, could the Joker Year One be a parody of the original history from Bob Kane and Bill Finger? (See the discussion of, Gulliver's Travels where Swift admits he intention to "vex" the readership.) In the opening passages of Year One edition #142, an anonymous narrator bewails his failure to succeed with a pallid corpse.Who is the narrator? Whose body is that?  And then, the PILL, the Red Mask Gang used to create three versions of the Joker, (and to dye their masks?). Who was the Red Mask, who did not inform the narrator of this error? Was there no other source of the dye? What Devil is the Narrator speaking of, and what is he hiding...only to be left empty when deceased? Zdarsky imagines  a meaningful conception in which a "virus" infecting everyone is made manifest when the Joker's Laugh is heard.This idea provides an apt description of the fundamentals of Epigenesis. And, where did Batman's accordion decorated uniform come from? Zdarsky took on a formidable task - retelling and fleshing out the Legend of the Batman/Joker developed over some eighty years, to produce an internally consistent whole. To this reader the result is convoluted, and desperate for an Introduction written by a scholar in a dingy garret. But, the audience will demand - "This is great!!!" Well, one saving grace is the Art and the word rectangles inserted in the art. Zdarsky makes a valiant effort and blended many of his skills to produce an admirable result. Like Swift's, Gulliver's Travels, the Batman/Joker yarn ends up as a fact based telling mixed with cleaver parody and satire. Zdarsky, creates a literary work contributing a enjoyable experience for those willing to apply themselves to the reading and to provide analytical thought, thereafter.   

Tangentially, one is reminded here of Friedrich Nietzsche in his Genealogy of Morals (1887) who wrote that morals were invented by common people envious of those far more successful.

           Lest we forget, who was right, Descartes or Locke?  Neither, they were                                                                            asking the wrong question.

                                       (June 21, 1957)

             "Just about every year, a visitor spends his summer in the small garden near the driveway. His name is "Gomphus," one of the "Club tail" dragonflies, I must say, as scientists have said, they "Fall in love..." with the objects of their studies, whether a chemical reaction, molecule, the universe or a small copper colored dragonfly - my good friend, Gomphus, and his family members who have visited me over the years. The scientists and I are not waxing, "Gooey" because the universe we find ourselves in is cold, distant and unfeeling - but the beauty of Natural Art is the saving grace of our sojourn here. I found Gomphus described on page 372 of my cherished volume,, "The Insect Book, (1901)  by Leland O Howard, PhD. This book I "borrowed" from my High School Library about 1953, and I will return it soon. I am sure you have many friends that visit your gardens, and you feel a closeness to them as I do. You are a cherished friend as well, and as you share pictures and adventures in Nature, we are immersed in the Art of this Beautiful Universe. I borrow this idea from the Existentialists, who maintain "you can make yourself as you prefer to be". 
            
                                           Conclusion:

Given all the contentions recorded above, what can be said? Most directly, the human identity is an" illusion", created by large numbers of molecules interacting in elaborate patterns (metabolism); yet, the identity emerges from these networks, without being synonymous with any one of  them alone. Wordsworth was wrong when he suggested nothing can regain the moment of "splendor in the grass." Instead, the "excitement" is initially brought about by the visual centers secreting "dopamine" which when transmitted to other parts of the brain "activates" them. On repeated exposure to the same stimuli, the secretion of dopamine diminishes, and so does the "excitement." This illusion of "identity" is an expression of the metabolism enabling the successful self replication of the information rich nucleic acids. Over time, "disorder" (entropy) develops in this system, the information cannot be effectively decoded, and the system disintegrates. Jonathan Miller (1978)  provided a suitable Metaphor - An orchestra and score are the metabolism and information of the body; a "person" is the melody played subject to improvisation.
